library(dplyr)

library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)

source(here("sample_size", "binary", "bin_corr_config.R"))

## What this shows

`bin_corr_results.qmd` summarises each run by one number per metric. This
report takes a single run (run **`r params$run`**, ρ = **`r params$rho`**) in
every scenario × sample size cell and plots every estimator's CATE unit by
unit, against the truth, across the trial population.

| Scenario | true CATE $\tau(x)$, a risk difference |
|---|---|
| 1: No HTE | $b_W$ |
| 2: Continuous HTE | $b_W + b_4 \tanh(X_4)$ |
| 3: Two vars + cts x cts | $b_W + b_3 X_3 + b_4 \tanh(X_4) + b_{45} \tanh(X_4) \tanh(X_5)$ |
| 4: Cosine HTE | $b_W + b_4 \cos(X_4)$ |

with control risk $m_0(x) = 0.34 + 0.36\,\mathrm{plogis}(b_0 + b_1 X_1 + b_2 X_2)$.
X4 drives the heterogeneity in scenarios 2–4, so it is the x axis throughout.
At ρ = 0.5 the prognostic X1, X2 are correlated with X3–X5, so the control
risk moves with the effect modifiers; the bias is also plotted against it.

A run is seeded by its run index alone, so at a given n the four scenarios
share W and the covariates: the differences down a column of panels are the
DGM, not the draw. Across n they are different datasets. The estimates are the
ones the metrics score: in-sample on the trial's own units (out-of-bag for the
forests, cross-fitted for the SuperLearner nuisances). The T-learners are
recovered from the DR learners' saved stage 1 (`R/metrics.R::t_learner_tau()`).

```{r data}
if (nzchar(params$res_path)) study$res_path <- params$res_path
RHO <- as.numeric(params$rho)
RUN <- as.integer(params$run)

SCENARIOS <- 1:4
N_LEVELS <- c(100, 250, 500, 1000)

# as bin_corr_results.qmd, so the reports read side by side
scenario_labels <- c(
  `1` = "1: No HTE",
  `2` = "2: Continuous HTE",
  `3` = "3: Two vars + cts x cts",
  `4` = "4: Cosine HTE"
)

# named, so a figure with a subset of models (the pseudo-outcomes) keeps each
# model's colour; in MODEL_LABELS order, which is the order drf_scale() gives
# them in bin_corr_results.qmd
MODEL_ORDER <- c("dr_oracle", "dr_semi_oracle", "dr_random_forest",
                 "dr_superlearner", "causal_forest", "t_random_forest",
                 "t_superlearner")
MODEL_COLOURS <- setNames(
  as.character(paletteer::paletteer_d("rcartocolor::Safe")[seq_along(MODEL_ORDER)]),
  MODEL_LABELS[MODEL_ORDER]
)

# the DR learners' pseudo-outcomes: where each one's po is saved
PO_SOURCES <- list(
  dr_oracle = c("dr_oracle", "po"),
  dr_semi_oracle = c("dr_semi_oracle", "po"),
  dr_random_forest = c("nuisances_rf", "po"),
  dr_superlearner = c("nuisances_sl", "po")
)

cells <- expand.grid(scenario = SCENARIOS, n = N_LEVELS)
cells$file <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(cells)), function(i) {
  file.path(combo_dir(study, list(rho = RHO, scenario = cells$scenario[i],
                                  n = cells$n[i])),
            paste0("res_sim_", RUN, ".RDS"))
}, character(1))
cells$found <- file.exists(cells$file)

#' One run's per-unit estimates and pseudo-outcomes, in long form
read_cell <- function(scenario, n, file) {
  sim_res <- readRDS(file)
  d <- sim_res$data
  units <- tibble(scenario = scenario, n = n, unit = seq_len(nrow(d)),
                  W = d$W, Y = d$Y, X1 = d$X1, X2 = d$X2, X3 = d$X3,
                  X4 = d$X4, X5 = d$X5, p0 = sim_res$truth$p0,
                  tau_true = sim_res$truth$tau)

  taus <- lapply(intersect(names(sim_res), CATE_MODELS),
                 function(m) sim_res[[m]]$tau)
  names(taus) <- intersect(names(sim_res), CATE_MODELS)
  t_src <- c(t_random_forest = "nuisances_rf", t_superlearner = "nuisances_sl")
  for (m in names(t_src)) {
    nuis <- sim_res[[t_src[[m]]]]
    if (!is.null(nuis$po) && !is.null(nuis$Y.hat)) {
      taus[[m]] <- t_learner_tau(nuis, d$Y, d$W)
    }
  }
  est <- bind_rows(lapply(names(taus), function(m) {
    mutate(units, model = m, tau_hat = taus[[m]])
  }))

  pos <- bind_rows(lapply(names(PO_SOURCES), function(m) {
    po <- sim_res[[PO_SOURCES[[m]][1]]][[PO_SOURCES[[m]][2]]]
    if (is.null(po) || is.null(taus[[m]])) return(NULL)
    mutate(units, model = m, po = po, tau_hat = taus[[m]])
  }))

  list(est = est, po = pos)
}

loaded <- pmap(cells[cells$found, c("scenario", "n", "file")], read_cell)

label_cells <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(model = factor(MODEL_LABELS[model], levels = MODEL_LABELS[MODEL_ORDER]),
           scenario_lab = factor(scenario_labels[as.character(scenario)],
                                 levels = scenario_labels),
           n_lab = factor(paste("n =", n), levels = paste("n =", N_LEVELS))) %>%
    droplevels()
}

est <- bind_rows(map(loaded, "est")) %>%
  mutate(bias = tau_hat - tau_true) %>%
  label_cells()
po <- bind_rows(map(loaded, "po")) %>% label_cells()
```

```{r missing-cells, results="asis"}
if (!all(cells$found)) {
  miss <- cells[!cells$found, ]
  cat("**Not found, left out:** ",
      paste0("scenario ", miss$scenario, ", n = ", miss$n, collapse = "; "),
      " (looked for `res_sim_", RUN, ".RDS` under `", study$res_path, "`).\n",
      sep = "")
}
```

```{r plot-helpers, include=FALSE}
house_style <- function() {
  list(scale_colour_manual(values = MODEL_COLOURS, drop = FALSE),
       drf_theme(),
       theme(legend.position = "bottom"))
}

# points are many (up to 1000 per panel), so faint
PT_ALPHA <- 0.35

# the truth as a black layer on top of a model's points. In scenarios 1, 2 and
# 4 tau depends on X4 alone, so it draws as a curve; in scenario 3 it also
# depends on X3 and X5, so it is a band
truth_layer <- function(df) {
  geom_point(data = distinct(df, scenario_lab, n_lab, unit, X4, tau_true),
             aes(x = X4, y = tau_true), colour = "black", size = 0.5,
             inherit.aes = FALSE)
}
```

## This run's metrics

`R/metrics.R::cate_metrics()` on the run shown, i.e. the numbers
`bin_corr_results.qmd` averages. Where `bin_corr_metrics.RDS` is in the
results folder, *MSE percentile* places this run's MSE among all runs of its
cell for that model (50 = a typical run, high = a bad one).

```{r run-metrics}
run_metrics <- est %>%
  group_by(scenario, scenario_lab, n, model) %>%
  summarise(cate_metrics(tau_hat, tau_true, first(scenario)), .groups = "drop")

metrics_file <- file.path(study$res_path, "bin_corr_metrics.RDS")
if (file.exists(metrics_file)) {
  all_mse <- readRDS(metrics_file) %>%
    filter(rho == RHO, scenario %in% SCENARIOS) %>%
    mutate(model = factor(MODEL_LABELS[model], levels = MODEL_LABELS[MODEL_ORDER])) %>%
    select(scenario, n, model, run, mse)
  pctile <- all_mse %>%
    group_by(scenario, n, model) %>%
    summarise(mse_pctile = if (RUN %in% run) {
      100 * mean(mse <= mse[run == RUN], na.rm = TRUE)
    } else NA_real_, .groups = "drop")
  run_metrics <- left_join(run_metrics, pctile, by = c("scenario", "n", "model"))
} else {
  run_metrics$mse_pctile <- NA_real_
}

run_metrics %>%
  arrange(scenario, n, mse) %>%
  select(scenario_lab, n, model, bias, ate_bias, rmse, corr, sign_acc, mse_pctile) %>%
  kable(digits = 3,
        col.names = c("Scenario", "n", "Model", "Bias", "ATE bias", "RMSE",
                      "Correlation", "Sign accuracy", "MSE percentile"))
```

## Estimated CATE across the population

Each model's estimates (coloured) against X4, with the true CATE in black and
0 dashed. One y scale per scenario, so the models and sample sizes compare
directly. In scenario 3 the truth also depends on X3 and X5, so it is a band
rather than a curve.

```{r cate-x4, results="asis", fig.height=14}
for (s in levels(est$scenario_lab)) {
  df <- filter(est, scenario_lab == s)
  cat("\n\n### ", s, "\n\n", sep = "")
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = X4, y = tau_hat, colour = model)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(alpha = PT_ALPHA, size = 0.8) +
    truth_layer(df) +
    facet_grid(rows = vars(model), cols = vars(n_lab)) +
    house_style() +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    labs(title = paste0("Estimated CATE, ", s, " (run ", RUN, ", ρ = ", RHO, ")"),
         x = "X4", y = "CATE (risk difference)")
  print(p)
}
```

## Estimated against true CATE

Scenarios 2–4; the dashed line is estimate = truth. Scenario 1's truth is a
single value, so its spread is all in the panels above. A cloud flatter than
the diagonal is shrinkage towards the ATE; one shifted off it is bias in the
ATE.

```{r cate-vs-true, results="asis", fig.height=14}
for (s in setdiff(levels(est$scenario_lab), scenario_labels[["1"]])) {
  df <- filter(est, scenario_lab == s)
  cat("\n\n### ", s, "\n\n", sep = "")
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = tau_true, y = tau_hat, colour = model)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(alpha = PT_ALPHA, size = 0.8) +
    facet_grid(rows = vars(model), cols = vars(n_lab)) +
    house_style() +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    labs(title = paste0("Estimated vs true CATE, ", s),
         x = "True CATE", y = "Estimated CATE")
  print(p)
}
```

## Pointwise bias across the population

Unit bias (estimate − truth) with a loess smooth per model, all models in one
panel per cell, so where in the population each one goes wrong reads off
together. Points are left out here; the smooth is the systematic part, and the
spread around it is in the next section.

```{r bias-x4, fig.height=11}
ggplot(est, aes(x = X4, y = bias, colour = model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(scenario_lab), cols = vars(n_lab), scales = "free_y") +
  house_style() +
  labs(title = "Smoothed pointwise bias against X4", x = "X4",
       y = "Bias (estimate − truth)", colour = "Model")
```

Against the control risk $m_0(x)$ instead: estimates pulled towards the
prognosis, rather than the effect modifiers, show up here.

```{r bias-p0, fig.height=11}
ggplot(est, aes(x = p0, y = bias, colour = model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(scenario_lab), cols = vars(n_lab), scales = "free_y") +
  house_style() +
  labs(title = "Smoothed pointwise bias against the control risk",
       x = "Control risk m0(x)", y = "Bias (estimate − truth)", colour = "Model")
```

## Distribution of pointwise bias

The spread of the unit biases within the run, per model. A box off 0 is
ATE-level bias; a tall box is unit-level error the run's mean bias hides.

```{r bias-box, fig.height=11}
ggplot(est, aes(x = n_lab, y = bias, colour = model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "transparent", outlier.size = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~scenario_lab, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  house_style() +
  labs(title = "Unit bias within the run", x = "Sample size",
       y = "Bias (estimate − truth)", colour = "Model")
```

## DR pseudo-outcomes

What the DR learners' second stage regresses on X: the pseudo-outcome (faint
points), the resulting DR estimate (coloured) and the true CATE (black). With a
binary Y and W.hat near 0.5 the residual term (Y − Ŷ)(W − Ŵ) / (Ŵ(1 − Ŵ)) puts
each pseudo-outcome of order ±1 from the truth, against an HTE of a few
hundredths, so the second stage is smoothing a very noisy target. The y axis is cut to the central 98% of the pseudo-outcomes.

```{r pseudo-outcomes, results="asis", fig.height=10}
for (s in levels(po$scenario_lab)) {
  df <- filter(po, scenario_lab == s)
  lims <- quantile(df$po, c(0.01, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE)
  cat("\n\n### ", s, "\n\n", sep = "")
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = X4)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(aes(y = po), colour = "grey60", alpha = 0.25, size = 0.6) +
    geom_point(aes(y = tau_hat, colour = model), size = 0.8) +
    truth_layer(df) +
    facet_grid(rows = vars(model), cols = vars(n_lab)) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = lims) +
    house_style() +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    labs(title = paste0("DR pseudo-outcomes and estimates, ", s),
         x = "X4", y = "Pseudo-outcome / CATE")
  print(p)
}
```
